name: Diploma PLC

corporate_actions.event: FY2025 results (YE 30-Sep-2025): revenue GBP1,524.5m (+12%), organic +11%, adj. operating profit GBP342.7m (+20%)
H1 2026 results: organic +15%, margin 24.5%, FY26 guidance upgraded to 12% organic, 6% acquisitions, ~25% margin
FY2026 results due mid/late November 2026 (after valuation date)

geography.fx_notes: North America 53%, Europe 19%, UK 18%, Australia/other 10% (pro forma for M&A to 18-Nov-2025). Reports in GBP; ~USD 50%+ translation exposure. China not disclosed (INFERENCE: immaterial).

kpis.value: Controls +26%, Seals +2%, Life Sciences +4% (H1 FY26); FY25: Controls +20%, Seals +2%, LS +6%

kpis.name: Leverage
kpis.value: 0.8x net debt/EBITDA at H1; slightly >1x pro forma for post-period deals; policy <2x

lease.source_id: not extracted this run (annual report cash-flow statement not fetched)

acquisitions.notes: Further ~GBP170m deals early H2 FY26. LTM to May-2026: 15 deals, GBP310m committed for ~GBP40m annualised EBIT = ~8x EBIT (company)
Peerless Aerospace Fastener (US) acquired in FY2025 and is the main organic driver in Controls; spend not extracted

management.senior_turnover_5y: CFO changed during 2024 (not re-verified); CEO stable since 2019
management.guidance_record: Strong: FY25 beat; FY26 guidance raised from 6%/22.5% (Nov-25) to 9% then 12% organic and ~25% margin (May-26)

evidence: Specialist components, consumables and aftermarket seals/fasteners/cable sold in small tickets [S2]
Seals aftermarket resilient (+2% in tough UK) [S1]
A.rationale: Largely consumable/MRO and specification-driven revenue across many customers, though Controls has cyclical project elements.

evidence: Value-add distribution with ability to pass on inflation via price [S1]
Operating margin expanded to ~25%, well above distribution peers [S1]
B.rationale: Specification, kitting and technical service create switching costs evidenced by pricing power and margins.

C.rationale: Niche-scale economics visible in rising margins and returns, though partly cyclical tailwind.

D.rationale: Large fragmented runway with evidenced high returns on acquired capital.

evidence: Consistent double-digit EPS growth track record [S1]

G.rationale: Disciplined M&A with evidenced returns; some concentration risk in Peerless.

evidence: Some catalogue items exposed to e-commerce
Windy City Wire (low-voltage cable) and IS Group interconnect serve non-residential buildings incl. data centres; share not disclosed
I2.rationale: INFERENCE: probably 5-10% indirect data-centre exposure via Controls; undisclosed.

I4.rationale: Value pricing suggests savings largely retained.

K.rationale: Reasonable but adjusted-profit focus and serial M&A add adjustments.

ai.notes: Not disclosed. INFERENCE: indirect data-centre exposure through Windy City Wire/IS Group (Controls) possibly mid-single digit % of group; semis immaterial.

sector_specific.notes: acquisition_growth_pct = H1 FY26 net acquisition contribution (FACT); FY26 guide 6% (TARGET). Construction: Windy City Wire tied to US non-residential construction; group share not disclosed. Serial acquirer: ~8x EBIT, ROATCE 22.7%. Peerless (aerospace fasteners) is a concentration of organic growth.

gates.notes: G1: 0.8x (~1x pro forma). G3: Peerless largest growth driver but share of revenue not disclosed (INFERENCE <15%). G4: company conversion ~90% annual typical, 76% H1; verify centrally. G5: AI/DC not disclosed, inferred <15%; flag for monitoring. G7: UK 18%, B2B.

bull_points: Organic growth accelerated to 11% (FY25) and 15% (H1 FY26) with margin at ~25% (S1, S2)
Acquisitions at ~8x EBIT with ROATCE 22.7% show value-creating compounding (S1)
Low leverage (~1x) leaves capacity for the raised 6% acquisition contribution (S1)
bear_points: Growth concentrated in Controls/Peerless (aerospace) with management saying margins are 'towards the top end' (S1)
UK Seals remains weak; ex-Peerless organic only high single digit (S1)
Possible indirect data-centre/non-res construction cyclicality via Windy City Wire is undisclosed
thesis_breakers: Group organic growth below 3% for a full year
ROATCE falling below 15% (the bottom of the stated high-teens range)
Average acquisition multiple rising above ~12x EBIT
